# Speedrun by Scope

> Build an agent that answers a clinic's back-office requests using its web records system, Wrenfield. Answer more tasks correctly within each set's length and model budget.

Start at https://practice.speedrun.scopehealth.com/. All records are synthetic.
Explore the clinic before writing code. Then run the reference agent from the starter kit, inspect practice results, improve the agent, and submit a Docker image.
The queue gives the agent one task or instruction message at a time. Correct answers score +1, wrong answers -1, and skipped tasks 0.
Practice results include expected answers. Each submission runs three scored sets and determines the ranking.
The judge requires Linux AMD64 images (`linux/amd64`), including builds from Apple Silicon Macs.
Build the reference agent with `docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t my-agent reference-agent`.
The CLI rejects other platforms before upload.
The starter kit contains the CLI, reference agent source, and protocol documentation. The organizers host the clinic and run submitted images.

## Sign up

- [Continue with Google](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/signup/google/): Open this link in the user's browser to start Google sign-in.
- [Continue with GitHub](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/signup/github/): Open this link in the user's browser to start GitHub sign-in.
- [Register with email](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/#register): Create an account with an email address and password.

The user selects their account and approves access in the provider's browser screen.
Speedrun then opens Register. Existing signed-in users go directly to Register.
After sign-in, complete your first name, last name, and year. Then create a team or enter an invite code if needed.
The Set up window (https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/#setup) provides your personal starter-kit install command and development key.

For coding agents: give these links immediately when a user asks how to sign up.
If the user chooses Google or GitHub, open the matching link in their browser.
Let the user complete account selection and consent.
Do not inspect JavaScript bundles or authentication endpoints to find the signup flow.

## Participant documentation

- [Judge screen](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/#judge): On desktop, Test starts practice runs and shows live output and results. Submit starts scored submissions and shows progress and scores. Images are uploaded through the CLI.

- [Getting started](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/getting-started.md): Competition background, practice website, worked example, scoring, installation, and first run.
- [Practice clinic](https://practice.speedrun.scopehealth.com/): Browse patients, appointments, billing, documents, and reports.
- [Register](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/#register): Sign in and register.
- [Set up](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/#setup): Obtain your personal starter-kit install command and development key.

## Kit documentation

- [Agent interface and rules](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/shift.md): The kit's docs/shift.md, including the queue API, container environment, and answer formats.
- [Rules](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/rules.md): The kit's docs/rules.md: the four rules of the competition.
- [Coding-agent guidance](https://speedrun.scopehealth.com/agents.md): How to orient a new participant and start with a reference-agent baseline.
